subject: Realtime latency spikes — request to preserve runtime logs and handling steps
messages:
From: Luke Barnes <luke@streamline.ai>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.example.com, olivia.svc@streamline.ai
Cc: Greg Thompson <gthompson@streamline.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Realtime latency spikes — request to preserve runtime logs and handling steps

Tessa —

We saw a recurring spike in latency and a cluster of 5xx errors between 2026-11-27T15:42:00Z and 2026-11-27T16:03:00Z that materially affected our production traffic (StreamlineAI). Our SREs captured traces pointing to Redwood endpoints returning 503/504 during that window.

For our audit and a pending regulatory inquiry we need:
- Confirmed preservation of all runtime logs, request traces, and KV cache telemetry for the timeframe above (request IDs included).
- Details on how logs are retained, whether anything is rotated or deleted automatically, and the exact retention cutoff for our org.
- A chain-of-custody note showing who accessed or exported logs during and after the incident.

Can you (a) confirm those artifacts will be preserved intact as-is, (b) tell us where we can download a signed package for the window, and (c) give an ETA? We may need the package in a compliance-friendly format (signed manifest, MD5/SHA256 checksums).

This is time-sensitive — our compliance team has asked us to file an incident report tomorrow morning (PST). Looping Olivia and Greg for legal.

Thanks,
Luke
Director of Platform
StreamlineAI
From: tessa_morgan@redwood.example.com
To: Luke Barnes <luke@streamline.ai>, Olivia Chen <olivia.svc@streamline.ai>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.example.com, monica_patel@redwood.example.com, markus_klein@redwood.example.com
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 16:23:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Realtime latency spikes — request to preserve runtime logs and handling steps

Luke —

Thanks for the heads up and the clear window. I'm escalating this now to SRE and Security. Short answers up front: yes, we will preserve the raw artifacts from that timeframe and produce a signed manifest; we can export them to a secure, read-only bucket and provide checksums.

Next steps I’m taking:
- Rishi (SRE) — please snapshot the runtime logs, request traces, and KV cache state for 2026-11-27T15:30:00Z to 2026-11-27T16:15:00Z and export to a compliance bucket. Include request IDs and any transporter/edge logs.
- Monica (SRE lead) — confirm retention policy and whether any automatic rotation affected those shards; if retention would have deleted anything we will run retrieval from cold storage.
- Markus (Security) — please advise on chain-of-custody packaging and whether we should produce a signed audit package for StreamlineAI’s legal.

Luke, I’ll reply with an ETA within 90 minutes and attach the manifest when ready.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Lead — Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.example.com
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.example.com, monica_patel@redwood.example.com, markus_klein@redwood.example.com
Cc: Luke Barnes <luke@streamline.ai>, Olivia Chen <olivia.svc@streamline.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 16:48:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Realtime latency spikes — request to preserve runtime logs and handling steps

On Fri, Nov 27, 2026 at 4:23 PM Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.example.com> wrote:
> Luke —
> Thanks for the heads up...

All — quick technical status:
- Snapshot completed for the range 2026-11-27T15:30:00Z -> 2026-11-27T16:15:00Z. Artifacts captured:
  * Inference runtime logs (per-host rotated logs) — consolidated into runtime_log_manifest_20261127.csv (attached).
  * Request traces (tracing-id list) with span details and sampling metadata.
  * Edge/load-balancer HTTP logs (including 5xx responses).
  * KV cache metrics and last-known prefixes for affected pods.
- Default tenant retention is 30 days; however, we have not auto-pruned the snapshot artifacts (we executed a point-in-time export before rotation).
- Export location: s3://redwood-compliance/exports/streamline/dl-3947/20261127/ (read-only, restricted). We will generate signed URLs for delivery.

Attached: runtime_log_manifest_20261127.csv (list of files and MD5 checksums), s3_export_instructions.txt (how to download), preliminary_trace_index.txt (first 500 request IDs).

Action items now:
- Markus: please package the artifacts with a signed manifest and provide chain-of-custody steps/proof.
- Tessa: confirm if Streamline wants the package on our secure share or delivered to their S3.

ETA for signed package: 3 hours (depending on packaging and legal review).

—Rishi
SRE — Redwood Inference
From: markus_klein@redwood.example.com
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.example.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.example.com, monica_patel@redwood.example.com
Cc: Luke Barnes <luke@streamline.ai>, Greg Thompson <gthompson@streamline.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 18:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Realtime latency spikes — request to preserve runtime logs and handling steps

On Fri, Nov 27, 2026 at 4:48 PM Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.example.com> wrote:
> All — quick technical status:
> - Snapshot completed...

Thanks — and a few security/forensics notes:
- Chain-of-custody: we'll create an audit package that includes a signed manifest (SHA256), an access log snapshot (who/what accessed the export path), and a packaging report (timestamped by our HSM-backed signing service).
- Redaction guidance: we will not redact any request IDs or timestamps unless Streamline requests PII redaction. If they need redaction for GDPR/DSAR reasons, we’ll coordinate with their legal.
- Evidence format options: (1) a gzipped TAR with manifest + checksums + .sig, (2) a signed S3 export with server-side encryption enabled and an access-control audit trail.
- Retention/restore: while tenant retention is 30 days by default, exports moved to the compliance bucket are retained indefinitely per export policy for escalations.

I will prepare the audit_package_instructions.pdf and the signed manifest. Expect the package and access details no later than 2026-11-28T09:30:00-08:00.

Markus Klein
Head of Security
Redwood Inference
From: Luke Barnes <luke@streamline.ai>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.example.com
Cc: Olivia Chen <olivia.svc@streamline.ai>, Greg Thompson <gthompson@streamline.ai>, markus_klein@redwood.example.com
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Realtime latency spikes — request to preserve runtime logs and handling steps

Thanks, Tessa / team — that timeline works.

Two quick follow-ups from our side:
1) Can you confirm whether the export will include raw binary payloads (we'd prefer request/response headers and timings but would request stripping raw user payloads unless required).
2) Our legal (Greg Thompson) will connect separately to align on the packaging format and chain-of-custody wording. Please copy me on that thread.

Appreciate the quick response.

—Luke
From: tessa_morgan@redwood.example.com
To: Luke Barnes <luke@streamline.ai>, Greg Thompson <gthompson@streamline.ai>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.example.com, monica_patel@redwood.example.com, markus_klein@redwood.example.com, marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 10:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Realtime latency spikes — request to preserve runtime logs and handling steps

Luke —

Confirming: default export excludes raw request bodies unless you explicitly request them. We will include headers, timings, request IDs, and traces. If you need raw payloads, let us know and we will coordinate redaction/transfer controls.

Greg — I’ll loop you and Markus to finalize packaging language.

ETA still: audit package + signed manifest delivered to the secure share by 2026-11-28T09:30:00-08:00 (which is live now in the link I sent).

Thanks,
Tessa
